relations.subject: index:index-redistribution-setting
relations.evidence: Whether to redistribute indexes on rebalance. When true, Couchbase Server redistributes indexes when rebalance occurs, in order to optimize performance. When false (the default), such redistribution does not occur.

relations.subject: index:file-based-index-rebalancing
relations.evidence: Selects the index rebalance method. See [Index Rebalance Methods](/server/8.0/learn/clusters-and-availability/rebalance.html#index-rebalance-methods). If false (the default), Index Service nodes rebuild indexes that are newly assigned to them during a rebalance. If true, Couchbase Server moves a reassigned index's files between Index Service nodes.

relations.evidence: If set to true, when you create an index, you can use the WITH clause to specify which node should contain the index. However, when you alter an index, you cannot use the WITH clause to specify which node should contain the index.

relations.subject: index:index-storage-setting
relations.evidence: plasma (the default) — Sets the index storage mode to use the Plasma storage engine, which can utilize both memory and persistent storage for index maintenance and index scans.

relations.subject: index:index-storage-setting
relations.evidence: memory\_optimized — Sets the index storage mode to use memory optimized Global Secondary Indexes, which can perform index maintenance and index scan faster at in-memory speeds.

relations.subject: index:index-storage-setting

relations.subject: index:index-storage-setting

notable_absence.finding: The Security section names two specific privileges by prose ('Cluster Read and Bucket INDEX List privileges') alongside the two RBAC roles, but Server's RBAC catalogue (learn/security/roles.md) has no separately enumerable privilege tier - per the registry's own requiresServerRole predicate definition, a Server access requirement is always modeled as a role, never a requiresPrivilege relation (that predicate's range is reserved for Capella's privilege:capella-*-access-* catalogue). This page is a second piece of evidence that Server's docs sometimes talk in privilege-shaped language ('Cluster Read', 'Bucket INDEX List') without there being any corresponding first-class privilege concept to attach it to - the finding is dropped as a relation and recorded here instead, per the context file's instruction not to paraphrase or reconstruct evidence that doesn't fit an existing predicate's declared range.

cross_component_finding: This page states settings changes 'automatically propagate to all Index Service nodes, and will be remembered across node and cluster restarts' - i.e. persistent, cluster-wide, REST-configured settings for GSI. This is worth checking against fts:manager-options-endpoint's Search-service settings surface (round 23) during reconciliation: if that page does not make the same restart-durability claim, it would be a real, evidenced contrast in how the Index Service and the Search Service persist REST-configured settings.
cross_product_finding: None identified on this page - it documents only the Server-side Index Service REST surface, with no Capella- or other-product-facing statement to compare against.
